accounting.rationale: Defines the procedure basis for a defined assignment statement.
Introduces the conditions under which a subroutine defines x1 = x2.

requirements.title: A defined assignment statement is defined by a subroutine and ASSIGNMENT(=) generic interface
requirements.definition: A defined assignment statement is an assignment statement whose assignment is defined by a subroutine and a generic interface specifying ASSIGNMENT(=). The detailed generic interface and binding rules remain dependencies.

pending.type-bound-generic-control: PENDING positive-control source shape with a type-bound generic ASSIGNMENT(=) binding and a subroutine effect distinguishable from intrinsic component assignment.
pending.no-assignment-generic-exclusion: PENDING source-review or diagnostic/control shape showing that a same-looking subroutine without an ASSIGNMENT(=) generic does not define the assignment; the repaired control adds only the generic spec.
pending.non-subroutine-procedure-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control source shape attempting to use a non-subroutine procedure as assignment definition, repaired by replacing it with a subroutine of the same dummy signature.

requirements.title: A subroutine defines x1 = x2 when dummy, generic, type, and parameter conditions match
requirements.definition: A subroutine defines the defined assignment x1 = x2 only if it is specified by a SUBROUTINE or ENTRY statement with two dummy arguments d1 and d2, is provided through an ASSIGNMENT(=) generic interface or matching type-bound generic binding, has d1 and d2 types compatible with the dynamic types of x1 and x2, and has matching corresponding type parameters.

pending.two-dummy-subroutine-control: PENDING positive-control source shape using a two-dummy subroutine whose first dummy receives a distinguishable literal value derived from the second. The control must prove the subroutine, not intrinsic assignment, supplied the effect.
pending.entry-subroutine-control: PENDING source plan using an ENTRY statement only if the surrounding procedure rules are satisfied and the entry-specific effect is distinguishable. If ENTRY coverage is impractical, this facet remains pending.
pending.generic-interface-path-control: PENDING positive-control source shape where an ordinary generic interface with ASSIGNMENT(=) provides the subroutine and a literal effect is checked.
pending.type-bound-binding-path-control: PENDING positive-control source shape where the declared or dynamic type provides the matching type-bound generic binding and dispatch is observed through a distinct literal payload.
pending.dummy-type-incompatibility-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control source shape with d1 or d2 intentionally incompatible with x1 or x2 dynamic type, repaired by changing only that dummy type.
pending.type-parameter-mismatch-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control source shape with mismatched corresponding type parameters between dummy and actual assignment operands, repaired by matching the parameter values.

requirements.title: Defined-assignment rank matching has an elemental uniqueness alternative
requirements.definition: For a subroutine to define x1 = x2, either the ranks of x1 and x2 match those of d1 and d2, or the subroutine is elemental, x2 is scalar or has the same rank as x1, and no other subroutine defines the assignment.

requirements.title: Array dummy shapes and elemental defined assignments impose shape/conformance conditions
requirements.definition: If d1 or d2 is an array, the shapes of x1 and x2 shall match the shapes of d1 and d2 respectively. If the defining subroutine is elemental, x2 shall be conformable with x1.

review_rationale: batch106: independent fresh-context source review against pinned J3/24-007 (sha256 7371e889...). Reviewer read all 14 base units of 10.2.1.1, 10.2.1.2, 10.2.1.4 and 10.2.1.5 in the original PDF across pages 188 to 194, verified 14 base / 52 fine units, 21 requirements and 89 facets (all pending), and confirmed that only 12 base units are newly accounted because R1033 and C1015 were already counted. The central question was the ownership boundary with 10.2.1.3, which is already registered and sits in the middle of this scope with 26 base units and 144 facets. The reviewer read that catalogue and checked both failure directions. No duplication: the 10.2.1.2 p1 allocatable, character-kind and deferred-length plans admit the cases but leave the resulting allocation, length, bounds, truncation, padding, conversion and values to 10.2.1.3; the p3 pointer plans require an associated definable conforming target but leave the target write to 10.2.1.3 and association changes to 10.2.2; the 10.2.1.4 plans classify the subroutine, generic, rank and shape conditions and leave element-by-element interpretation to 10.2.1.5 and generic mechanics to 15.4.3.4.3. No gaps either: 10.2.1.1 p1 owns the partition rule rather than punting it, and 10.2.1.2 keeps every local eligibility condition including the intrinsic-not-defined classification, polymorphic restrictions, conformance and rank admission, BOZ destination type, Table 10.8, character kind compatibility, derived type parameter compatibility, coindexed restrictions, pointer target eligibility and the coarray unallocated-allocatable prohibition. The zero-permissions claim was independently adjudicated and accepted: no normative unit in scope grants processor latitude, and the sentence permitting pure elemental subroutine assignments to be performed simultaneously or in any order occurs only in the unnumbered NOTE in 10.2.1.5, correctly dispositioned informative, with plans forbidding order, simultaneity, temporary, side-effect and call-count oracles. Table 10.8 was read row by row from the table itself; all eight rows are owned, and the enum row preserves the condition that when expr is integer a primary in expr shall be an enumerator of the enum type, rather than admitting arbitrary integers. Character plans require explicit LEN checks and warn against relying on blank-padded comparison, and no plan assumes ISO 10646 or ASCII kinds exist. Decision: source-eligible, no blocking findings; two non-blocking observations recorded in doc/source_audits/batch_106.json. This registers source accounting only: it is not fixture approval, it supplies no execution, and it approves no oracle.
